output.answer: Aerodrome was rejected for the wide (±40%) cbBTC/WETH position because its emission mechanics make it unsuitable for wide ranges. In the gauge, a position earns only AERO emissions (0 fees — fees go to voters), and the emission APR is distributed across liquidity in the active tick ±1 tick (for CL10 ≈ a 0.3% band). The wide ±40% position's liquidity-per-dollar is ≈6.5 vs ≈1,300 for that 0.3% band, giving it only ~0.5% share, i.e. ≈4–6%/yr in AERO (CL100: ≈3.8%/yr). Uniswap ±40% offers ≈5–11%/yr in fees with no token to sell (AERO has 10.9%/yr inflation and FX risk). Aerodrome's richer pool (fee tier 0.075 vs 0.05 at the same volume, emissions ≈2× fees) helps only ultra-narrow, actively managed positions — the 'narrowing/chasing' class already falsified 26–31 Aug. Verdict: NO, no code, no capital; Uniswap remains the best venue for wide LP on this pair; closed permanently (like WETH/USDC on 02.09).

output.answer: On 17 August 2026 the project closed a .bot/pipeline incident through coordinated work across three sessions (Fable, CC-Win, CC-Mac). Two problems were involved: (1) the HomosPipeline Windows scheduled task (07:30) had most likely been broken since setup on 10 Aug — it ran as SYSTEM, causing a spawn npx ENOENT error; DefiLlama data had gone stale to 158 h and the selector honestly refused to propose from stale data, so no new proposals were produced for 5 days; and (2) a live-data risk: the .bot folder was tracked in git while a runner did git reset --hard every 3 minutes, which would overwrite live bot files with the repo version. Resolution: Fable flagged the risk; CC-Win took step 0 (robocopy backup + stop the runner), diagnosed the SYSTEM/ENOENT cause, switched the task to the elo account, and ran a manual fetch:llama; CC-Mac held the untrack until step 0 was confirmed (Fable cut the confirmation deadlock); then untrack commit f18f50e, pull, restore the backup, start the runner and restart the bot. Result: zero data loss. A follow-up 48 h TTL fix for stale OPEN/ROTATE proposals was also made, and on 18 Aug the risky auto-pull runner was withdrawn entirely.

output.answer: The package was pinned to exactly 1.0.0 (repo-wide, without a caret) on 19 Aug 2026 because of a Windows compatibility problem. Envio publishes the native win32 binary only up to version 1.0.0; newer versions (the caret range ^1.4.0 resolved to a wrapper without the native module) hard-throw on Windows, while macOS worked because darwin binaries are published up to 1.4.0. Since the API the project uses is identical in 1.0.0 (verified by a diff and in the npm registry), pinning to the exact version was preferred over the unused 1.x helpers, and a shared lockfile was favored. This fixed the HyperSync fetch pipeline that had been failing on all hs-* steps on the Windows machine.

output.answer: On Base cbBTC/WETH (0.05% fee tier), with 40-day walk-forward windows stepped every 10 days (33 windows: 4 up, 8 down, 21 flat), passive ±50% ("Pasywny ±50%") averaged +0.33% per window against HODL 50/50, with a 72.7% win rate (24 of 33 windows positive). Its worst window was -1.04% (in a down regime), best +1.44%. By regime: up (4 windows) win rate 25% (mean -0.11%); down (8 windows) win rate 25% (mean -0.44%, worst -1.04%); flat (21 windows) win rate 100% (mean +0.72%). So the edge is entirely in flat regimes; it underperforms HODL in trending up/down windows. Note: this exact 40d/10d setting had no saved result, so it was run live on the owner's machine today (run name run-j20261116T140040n1-walkforward-base-cbbtc-weth-005-365d-40d).

I ran the requested walk-forward (pool arbitrum-weth-usdc-030-365d, 35-day windows every 7 days, 48 windows: 7 up / 20 down / 21 flat). The default set has six strategies. Mean vs HODL per window: Pasywny ±50% +0.02; Adaptacyjna k=2 h=24h payback≤7d −0.51; Adaptacyjna k=3 h=24h payback≤7d −0.45; Adapt k=3 h=24h + trend(exit,HL7d,5%) +0.19; Adapt k=3 h=24h + trend(exit,HL7d,5%,vg1.4,t2=10%) −0.24; Adapt k=3 h=24h + trend(exit,HL7d,5%,re>ema) +0.21. Highest mean: Adapt k=3 h=24h + trend(exit,HL7d,5%,re>ema) at +0.21% vs HODL. No strategy had a worst window above −3%: the best worst was −7.01 (trend exit,HL7d,5%); the others were −11.63 (Pasywny ±50%), −10.18 (k=2), −12.33 (k=3), −8.24 (vg1.4,t2=10%), and −8.13 (re>ema). So no strategy met the project's 'worst > −3%' criterion on this pool.

output.answer: For Hyperliquid BTC funding carry with a 3.8%/yr USDC benchmark, 60-day windows stepped every 15 days (56 windows), the run shows a small positive mean edge of +0.06% per window (median +0.03%), a win rate of 55.4% of windows above zero, and a worst window of −0.87%. Annualized funding over the series was 11.76%/yr, but after the 50% capital share, 0.25% round-trip cost and the 3.8% benchmark, the breakeven funding per window is 1.75%. This is a fresh run of today's engine; note the project's earlier E8.1 carry test (30/90-day windows, 4.5% bench) had found no positive edge in any of 8 series, so this modest 60d result sits in a class the journal had closed as unprofitable.

output.answer: I ran a 30-day walk-forward on Base WETH/USDC (0.05% fee tier, 365d history) with a 10-day step (34 windows: 6 up, 12 down, 16 flat). Passive ±50% ("Pasywny ±50%") averaged -0.35% vs a 50/50 HODL per 30-day window, with a median of +0.99%, a 67.6% win rate, worst window -14.78% and best +3.01%. By regime: up windows mean +0.31% (83% win, worst -1.35%); down windows mean -3.61% (17% win, worst -14.78%); flat windows mean +1.86% (100% win, worst +0.70%). Its own APR quartiles: Q25 -73.6%, median +12.8%, Q75 +78.7%. In the last 90 days (6 windows) it averaged -0.40% with a 50% win rate. Against the script's criterion (winPct ≥ 65 and worst > -3) it passes on win rate (67.6%) but fails on the worst window (-14.78%).

No new run was needed: a saved walk-forward already covers Base cbBTC/WETH at 0.05% over 720 days with 30-day windows (47 windows, 15-day step). Passive ±50% ("Pasywny ±50%") beat its HODL 50/50 benchmark in 63.8% of windows, with mean -0.30% vs HODL, median +0.20%, worst -7.76%, best +1.30%. By regime it won in only one of three: flat windows 86.7% (mean +0.47%), down windows 33.3% (mean -0.47%), up windows 0% (mean -4.51%). Against the project's own soundness criterion (winPct >= 65 and worst > -3) it fails on both counts, and against the PLAN.md gate of winning in at least 2 regimes it wins in only 1. In the last 90 days it was positive in all 4 windows (mean +0.13%).

The journal's walk-forward tables for the same pool likewise report only Pasywny ±50%, Sztywny ±15%, and the adaptive strategies.
